messages:
maria: Quick idea — rather than a single canary flag, what if we store a preview snapshot of the runtime config and do a staged exposure that can be pinned from the console?
kevin: explain 'preview snapshot' — is that just a config diff we promote, or a separate read path?
maria: separate read path. snapshot lives alongside live config. routing layer can opt-in a % of traffic to read the snapshot. advantage: we can validate drift and telemetry before fully swapping the live config.
anjali: I like that. we should also attach an etag + applied_by metadata so ops can see who pinned it.
kevin: questions: how does this interact with quota tokens? if snapshot increases per-tenant quotas we could accidentally blow budget for small customers. need per-tenant caps on snapshot exposures.
sam: metric checklist proposal: per-route token rate, 95p latency, error rate, and a "delta drift" metric (snapshot vs baseline requests). if delta drift > threshold -> auto-revert.
dmitri: agree on auto-revert but add a circuit-breaker that triggers when aggregated cost delta > blast_cap. blast_cap = percentage of daily token budget across affected tenants.
anjali: UX: in console expose a "preview pin" button that shows diff, preview-population (N users sampled), and an estimated cost delta using historical traffic. think: small sparkline + toggle.
maria: implementation sketch: snapshot stored as JSON blob and an activation manifest: {
  "snapshot_id": "snap-20240523-42",
  "traffic_pct": 5,
  "ttl": 3600,
  "etag": "W/\"abc123\""
}  -- then routing checks manifest to route.
kevin: pseudo CLI to create: `rictl config snapshot create --from live --name=snap-42 --traffic=5 --ttl=1h`
kevin: service side: routing should honor per-tenant override table before snapshot; order: tenant-override > snapshot-route > live.
ops-bot: preflight-check: snapshot schema ok, no missing fields, manifest etag present.
sam: telemetry question — how do we surface the "delta drift"? need a sampling sidecar that captures both snapshot and live outputs for identical prompts. might be heavy. alternative: closed-loop eval on representative prompt set (N=200) every 10m.
dmitri: closed-loop eval sounds safer. also add a cheap KV-cache hit metric so we don't mistake better cache hit for model changes.
anjali: rollout plan proposal: 0.5% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with a 30m soak at each step and automated checks. console will show next-step ETA and pass/fail reason.
maria: what about API semantics? expose a preview header `X-RI-Preview: snap-20240523-42` to force a request to snapshot for debug.
kevin: +1 for header. also need admin-only scope for pinning snapshots.
sam: I'll draft telemetry dashboards: snapshot vs baseline comparison, cost delta estimate, regressions per-eval-prompt, and snapshot-apply history.
dmitri: rollback playbook: immediate rollback if: cost delta > blast_cap OR any critical error >= 1% OR eval regression score drops by > 5 points. otherwise manual roll forward.
maria: should we allow multi-snapshot stacking? e.g., routing snapshot + quantization snapshot. probably no, keep it single active snapshot per-route to reduce complexity.
kevin: can we do a dry-run mode that simulates routing decision without actually switching traffic? router logs an "intended target" field. ops can run replay to validate.
anjali: that's useful: `router.intended_target` in logs + replay tool. console can show replay pass rate.
kevin: tiny nit: ensure snapshots are immutable once created (only manifest can change traffic_pct/ttl). helps audit.
maria: next steps: kevin to prototype routing-side check + header, anjali to mock console UX, sam telemetry dashboard, dmitri rollback thresholds. i'll coordinate a short sync on friday. :thumbsup:
kevin: 👍
anjali: sounds good
dmitri: added to my board
sam: will put dashboard links in the thread when ready
ops-bot: scheduled sync created: #eng-platform -> Friday 10:30am (calendar invite sent)
